disclaimer: Provided as is, without warranty of any kind. Compiled by hand from manufacturer specifications, EPA listings and published reviews; it may contain errors or omissions, and figures correct when verified may since have changed. Verify against the manufacturer before relying on any value. No liability is accepted for any use of this data.

models.notes: Offered only for model year 2024 — Acura discontinued the ZDX nameplate in September 2025. Built on GM's Ultium platform, shared with the Honda Prologue.

Type S adds Brembo brakes, adaptive air suspension, 22-inch wheels, Hands Free Cruise, and a head-up display over A-Spec. Acura hasn't published an exact 0-60 time — reviewers cite "just under 5 seconds." Offered only for model year 2024 before the ZDX nameplate was discontinued in September 2025.

Single-motor RWD entry trim, renamed from '40' to '45 e-tron' for 2025 with a larger 82 kWh pack. No frunk — a deep rear underfloor well instead. Heat pump isn't available on this trim (only on the 55 e-tron quattro, via the Cold Weather Package).
No SQ4 e-tron performance model exists — this dual-motor 55 e-tron quattro is the top powertrain available for Q4 e-tron. Heat pump is available via the optional Cold Weather Package (not standard).

First Audi EV on the PPE platform, shared with the Porsche Macan Electric. Battery is marketed as a 100 kWh pack; usable capacity is closer to ~95 kWh. The no-cost Ultra package adds a heated steering wheel and heated rear seats on some configurations. 456 hp is the launch-control peak (422 hp continuous).
Audi's original e-tron (MLB EV) platform SUV, being phased out. Native CCS1 charge port, with an Audi NACS DC adapter available as an accessory. Has a small frunk (no published cubic-foot figure).
Performance flagship of the Q6 e-tron line. 509 hp is the launch-control peak (483 hp / 631 lb-ft standard). Standard sport-tuned adaptive air suspension.

models.trim: S e-tron GT Premium Plus quattro
models.notes: Redesigned for 2025 and renamed 'S e-tron GT' in the US; 'Premium Plus' is the entry trim. 670 hp is the boost/launch-control peak (583 hp standard). Standard seats are synthetic leather.
912 hp / 2.4s 0-60 are with launch control engaged. RS e-tron GT Performance is the only RS trim for 2025.

Base RWD trim of BMW's 4 Series Gran Coupe-based liftback sedan. For 2026, BMW added silicon-carbide inverters, raising EPA range over the prior model year. Forward collision warning and lane departure warning are standard; full adaptive cruise and lane centering require the optional Driving Assistant Professional package. Charge port is CCS1 (adapter needed for Tesla Superchargers); no factory tow rating is published for the US.

For 2026, BMW replaced the prior i4 M50 with the more powerful M60 xDrive as the top i4 trim: 593 hp, dual-motor AWD, 130 mph top speed (140 mph with the optional High Performance Tire Package on 20-inch wheels). Driving Assistant Professional (adaptive cruise, lane centering) is an optional package, not standard.

As of March 2026 production, BMW switched the entire i5 lineup to a native NACS charge port with bundled J1772 and CCS1 adapters; earlier-built 2026 cars shipped with CCS1 and got a software update enabling Supercharger access. Blind spot detection, lane keeping assistant, forward collision mitigation, and speed limit assistant are standard; full adaptive cruise and lane centering require the optional Driving Assistant Professional package.
The i5 M60 xDrive was the first BMW sold in the US with a native NACS charge port (added for 2026); it ships with adapters for legacy CCS1/J1772 equipment.

Flagship long-wheelbase electric 7 Series sedan; rear seats don't fold, so there's no expanded cargo figure. Uses CCS1 for 2026 — BMW plans to add native NACS starting with the 2027 model year. Top speed and tow rating aren't published for the US market.
For 2026, the former 516-hp xDrive50 was replaced by the 536-hp xDrive60 as BMW's mid-tier iX. The iX has no frunk — its hood doesn't open. US tow rating is 3,500 lb with the factory tow package.
Top performance iX trim, replacing the prior M60 as BMW's flagship electric SUV. Torque reaches 811 lb-ft briefly under Launch Control (749 lb-ft sustained).

First US 'Neue Klasse' platform BMW, on sale starting September 25, 2026. 800V architecture with 400 kW max DC charging (10-80% in ~21 min) and a native NACS port; supports bidirectional (V2L/V2H) charging. Base MSRP of $61,500 excludes $1,350 destination/handling. At launch, ventilated front seats and heated rear seats aren't yet available (expected to be added later).
800V architecture supports up to 350 kW DC fast charging. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist with automatic lane change, not full self-driving) is standard.

Premium Sport adds power-opening front/rear doors, 24-inch wheels (up from 22-inch standard), and dual power captain's chairs over Luxury. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is standard.

102 kWh is Cadillac's published total pack rating; usable capacity is somewhat lower. RWD Lyriq isn't tow-rated; AWD adds a 3,500 lb tow rating. No frunk. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is offered, $25/month after the trial period.

Dual-motor AWD, 515 hp / 450 lb-ft, with 22-inch 'After Midnight' finish wheels standard on Sport. MSRP is approximate (~$62,590) — sources vary $62k-$65k. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is offered, $25/month after the trial period.

Optiq is AWD-only in the US — every trim gets standard dual-motor AWD (front motor primary, rear engages as needed). No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto — Cadillac EVs use Google built-in instead. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) comes with a complimentary 3-year trial, then $25/month (or $15/month bundled with OnStar Connected Services).

Mechanically identical to Luxury AWD; Sport differs mainly in styling (gloss-black exterior accents and dark badging vs. Luxury's Galvano Chrome trim). No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto — Google built-in only. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is offered, $25/month after the trial period.
Standard 11.5 kW onboard charger yields 305-mile EPA range. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is standard.

The optional 19.2 kW onboard charger trims EPA range slightly vs. the 11.5 kW unit on Luxury/Sport (300 vs. 305 mi). Adds Brembo front brakes, 22-inch Reverse Rim wheels, and a black-painted roof. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is standard.
Native CCS1 charge port for 2026, with an optional NACS Level 2 (AC-only) adapter — DC fast charging remains CCS1. Tow capacity of 1,500 lb requires the optional Trailering Provisions package.
Native CCS1 charge port for 2026; DC fast charging remains CCS1 (the optional NACS adapter is AC/Level 2 only).

First deliveries began around March 2026. Uses a new 65 kWh LFP (CATL) pack in a cell-to-pack design with a native NACS port. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto — this generation uses built-in Google infotainment instead. Super Cruise is confirmed as an optional hands-free highway driver-assist package on RS; whether it's also offered on LT hasn't been confirmed.

Mechanically identical to LT — RS is primarily an appearance package (gloss-black grille and roof rails, unique 17-inch gloss-black wheels), plus an optional Super Cruise hands-free highway driver-assist package. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto — this generation uses built-in Google infotainment instead.

Native CCS1 charge port for 2026 (GM has announced the 2027 Equinox EV switches to native NACS); an optional NACS AC adapter exists, but DC fast charging remains CCS1. Wireless phone charging is standard only on LT2/RS trims, not base LT1. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto — Google built-in infotainment instead. Super Cruise is available on LT2/RS, not on base LT.

Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is available as part of an optional Active Safety Package (~$3,355) on RS, not standard. RS AWD is offered with either an 11kW or 19kW onboard charger, with slightly different EPA range (307 vs. 288 mi); this entry uses the 11kW/307-mile configuration.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is a 10.7 cu ft front 'e-trunk' plus a 5'11" composite bed. WT Standard Range is the base configuration. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is offered. GM's Ultium DC fast-charge ceiling is 350 kW platform-wide; WT's standard onboard AC charger is 11 kW.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is a 10.7 cu ft front 'e-trunk' plus bed. RST is the range-topping trim with the 205 kWh Max Range Ultium pack. The 460-mile range figure is GM's own advertised estimate for RST (no RST-specific EPA-certified rating has been published). 754 hp / 785 lb-ft and the 4.5s 0-60 reflect RST's 'Wide Open Watts' launch-control peak; sustained output is lower. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is available. RST rides on adjustable Adaptive Air Ride suspension, so no single ground-clearance figure is published.

2-door liftback body with hatchback-style cargo access. 630 hp continuous, up to 670 hp for ~15 seconds via PowerShot mode (627 lb-ft). Range varies by wheel/tire package (216-279 mi across configurations); figures shown are for the highest-range 305/35ZR20 setup.

2-door liftback body with hatchback-style cargo access. 496 hp includes the factory Direct Connection Stage 1 upgrade (404 lb-ft base). Dodge discontinued the R/T trim for 2026 — the electric Charger Daytona lineup is now Scat Pack/Scat Pack Plus only; this reflects the last MY2025 R/T AWD specs. Range varies by wheel/tire package (268-308 mi); figures shown are for the highest-range 255/45R20 setup.

Base (500e)RED trim; four higher-priced special-edition trims (Inspired By Music, Inspired By Beauty, Inspired By Los Angeles, Giorgio Armani Edition) are also offered. Small 2-door/4-passenger city car with 7.5 cu ft of cargo space. US sales have been very low (roughly 1,141 units in 2025), and the model's future in the US market is uncertain. Lane Keeping Assist and Adaptive Cruise Control are optional, not standard, on this trim.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is the 14.1 cu ft 'Mega Power Frunk' plus the 5.5 ft bed. For 2026, Ford dropped the Standard Range battery, so all Lightning trims now use the 123 kWh Extended Range pack as standard: 580 hp / 775 lb-ft, ~3.8s 0-60. BlueCruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is available. Level 2 AC charging can be optioned up to 19.2 kW with the dual onboard charger.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is the 14.1 cu ft 'Mega Power Frunk' plus the 5.5 ft bed. Platinum uses the 131 kWh Extended Range battery. Towing is 8,600 lb standard, up to 10,000 lb with the optional Max Trailer Tow Package. Standard 22-inch wheels reduce range versus smaller wheel options. BlueCruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is available.

Select RWD uses the Standard Range 75.7 kWh (68 kWh usable) pack. The Mach-E uses a native CCS1 port (not NACS); a NACS-to-CCS1 adapter is a separate ~$200 accessory. For 2026, the frunk (4.8 cu ft) became a $495 option rather than standard equipment, and BlueCruise, the wireless charging pad, and the 360-degree camera moved from standard to optional on Select. Top speed is 112 mph. Seats are Ford's synthetic 'ActiveX' leatherette — no genuine leather is offered on any Mach-E trim.

Premium sits between Select and GT, available RWD or AWD; this entry is the AWD + Extended Range (91 kWh usable) configuration. 346 hp / 428 lb-ft. DC fast charging is 150 kW on the Extended Range pack (Select's smaller Standard Range pack is limited to 115 kW). The wireless charging pad lost standard-equipment status for 2026 and is now bundled only in the optional Technology Package. Heated steering wheel, heated/ventilated front seats, and a 10-speaker Bang & Olufsen system are standard on Premium. Limited to 19-inch wheels (no 20/21-inch option, unlike Select and GT). Native CCS1 charge port.

GT is standard AWD with the Extended Range 98.8 kWh pack (88 kWh usable): 480 hp / 600 lb-ft. Edmunds' own test track measured 3.7s 0-60; Ford's claim with the optional GT Performance Upgrade (+100 lb-ft to 700 lb-ft) is 3.3s. Native CCS1 charge port; NACS Supercharger access requires Ford's separate ~$200 adapter. Ventilated seats are notably not offered on GT — only on Premium, despite GT being the top trim. Top speed is 124 mph.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is an 11 cu ft frunk plus a 5-foot bed. Tri-motor 3X makes up to 1,000 hp, with a 'Watts to Freedom' launch mode. Ground clearance is adjustable via GM's Adaptive Air Ride suspension (roughly 10.1-15.9 in depending on mode), so no single figure is published. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is included with a free 3-year trial. Bi-directional vehicle-to-load charging is new for 2026.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold. Elevation is the entry trim, offered with Standard, Extended, and Max Range battery packs — the Extended Range option adds up to 645 hp / 765 lb-ft and a 12,500 lb tow rating, well above this Standard Range configuration. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is available on Elevation. Standard CoreTec synthetic leather (not genuine); ventilated front seats and heated rear seats are available as options.

Pickup truck with no enclosed rear cargo hold. Denali is GMC's top luxury trim, shown here with the Extended Range battery (170 kWh usable). Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, not full self-driving) is standard on Denali. Adds Adaptive Air Ride suspension and a panoramic glass roof.
Offered as a single 'Advanced' AWD trim for 2025. Battery grew from 87.2 kWh (pre-facelift) to 94.5 kWh for the current facelifted version.
Offered as a single 'Advanced' AWD trim. An optional $6,800 Prestige package adds Nappa leather, a 15-speaker Lexicon audio system, a head-up display, and heated rear seats.

For 2025, Genesis's RWD entry trim is named 'Standard' — 'Advanced' trim is AWD-only. Base seats are synthetic (vegan) leather, not genuine. Uses CCS1 with a complimentary NACS adapter available from Genesis; 2026+ GV60 switches to a native NACS port.

A temporary 'Boost' mode raises output to 483 hp / 516 lb-ft for 10-second bursts; 429 hp is the steady-state rating shown here. Nappa leather and heated rear seats are standard. Uses CCS1; 2026+ GV60 switches to native NACS.

Built on GM's Ultium platform, sharing underpinnings with the Chevy Blazer EV and Cadillac Lyriq. No frunk — there's a small ~0.8 cu ft underfloor storage bin behind the rear cargo floor instead. All Prologue trims — EX, Touring, and Elite, FWD or AWD — share the same 1,500 lb max tow rating.
Top trim; adds a 360-degree camera, head-up display, ventilated front seats, and a heated steering wheel over EX. No frunk — a small underfloor bin only.

MSRP of $35,000 excludes the $1,600 destination/freight charge. AWD isn't offered on this specific SE Standard Range trim — it's available on other 2026 Ioniq 5 trims. Seats are cloth; no leather option at this trim. V2L is supported via an accessory exterior adapter at the charge port; the interior 120V household outlet is reserved for Limited/XRT. Heated front seats are standard, but heated steering wheel, heated rear seats, and ventilated seats aren't available on this trim. Not factory tow-rated — only the XRT trim (with optional hitch) is rated to tow, 2,700 lb.

Dual-motor AWD: 165 kW rear + 74 kW front motor (239 kW / 320 hp combined, 446 lb-ft). Seat material is Hyundai's synthetic 'H-Tex' leatherette, not genuine leather. V2L includes both the exterior charge-port adapter and the interior 120V household outlet on this trim. Not factory tow-rated — only XRT (with optional hitch) is tow-rated.
Standard Range battery is cited as 53 kWh gross; usable capacity is somewhat lower (estimates range roughly 48-53 kWh depending on source).
Heated rear seats aren't offered even on this top trim.

Assembled in the US (Georgia), eligible for full federal EV tax credit at launch. Base S trim seats 7 with a 2nd-row bench; Limited/Calligraphy trims swap in 2nd-row captain's chairs, reducing capacity to 6. Single-motor RWD; AWD is available on higher trims of the same model.

Calligraphy uses the 422-hp dual-motor Performance AWD powertrain shared with Limited and Calligraphy Design trims. 2nd row has captain's chairs (6-passenger); base S/SE/SEL trims offer a bench for 7.
Kona Electric is FWD-only in the US; no AWD variant is offered. SE uses the smaller 48.6 kWh standard-range battery/133-hp motor; Limited and N Line use the 64.8 kWh long-range pack/201-hp motor.
Kona Electric is FWD-only in the US; no AWD variant is offered. Limited uses the 64.8 kWh long-range pack (261 mi on standard 17-in wheels; 230 mi with optional 19-in wheels).

The Recon EV went on sale in the US/Canada in mid-2026. Currently only offered as the launch-exclusive Moab trim: 33-inch all-terrain tires, removable doors, Trail Rated badge, e-locker axle. EPA range of 222 mi came in below Jeep's earlier 230-mile target.
EPA range varies by tire choice: 294 mi with standard Falken all-season tires, 262 mi with optional Pirelli tires.
2026 'Light' trim is RWD-only — AWD becomes available starting with Light Long Range. Base MSRP excludes the $1,545 destination fee. Top speed is 115 mph; frunk volume is 1.8 cu ft.

GT-Line AWD is $53,000 ($48,700 GT-Line base + $4,300 AWD upcharge), excluding the $1,545 destination fee. Seat material is SynTex synthetic leather/suede — no genuine leather option is offered on EV6. 19-inch black alloy wheels are standard, 20-inch available. Top speed is 117 mph; frunk volume is 0.7 cu ft (reduced vs. RWD due to the front drive motor).

Standard configuration is 7-passenger with a 2nd-row bench (6-passenger captain's-chair layout is available on other RWD/AWD trims). No built-in/integrated booster seat is offered on the EV9 on any trim. 8 cupholders, 6 USB-C ports. Max DC charge rate is 235 kW; max cargo with all seats folded is 81.7 cu ft.

Wind AWD's standard seating is 7-passenger with a 2nd-row bench (6-passenger captain's-chair layout is standard on Light Long Range RWD, Land AWD, and GT-Line AWD instead). Dual-motor e-AWD with torque vectoring, 99.8 kWh battery shared with Land and GT-Line trims. 0-60 is 5.7s (Boost mode off) / 5.0s (Boost on). No built-in/integrated booster seat is offered on the EV9 on any trim. Max DC charge rate is 210 kW; frunk volume shrinks to 1.8 cu ft on AWD trims due to the added front motor.
2025 Niro EV ships with a native NACS charge port. Niro EV is FWD-only; no AWD variant is offered.
Wave adds Highway Driving Assist II (automatic lane changes), power-folding mirrors, sunroof, head-up display, and Harman/Kardon audio over the Wind. Niro EV is FWD-only; no AWD variant is offered.

First-ever battery-electric ES, arriving at dealers September 2026 as part of the redesigned eighth-generation ES lineup (alongside a carryover-style 350h hybrid). Base 'Premium' grade shown; a 'Luxury' grade is also offered. 307-mile range is on standard 19-inch wheels (292 mi with optional 21-inch wheels). MSRP of $47,610 is before the $1,395 delivery fee.

Dual-motor DIRECT4 AWD version of the first-ever battery-electric ES, arriving at dealers September 2026. Base 'Premium' grade shown; a 'Luxury' grade is also offered. 276-mile range is on standard 19-inch wheels (272 mi with optional 21-inch wheels). MSRP of $50,610 is before the $1,395 delivery fee.

Entry FWD trim of the redesigned-for-2026 RZ lineup (added alongside carryover 450e AWD and new 550e F SPORT AWD). Lexus Safety System+ 3.0 is standard: pre-collision system with pedestrian detection, adaptive cruise, and lane tracing assist. No frunk. 10-80% DC fast charge takes about 30 minutes. Battery warranty is 10 years / 150,000 miles (capacity retention above 70%). Interior is synthetic leather (not genuine) with a heated steering wheel standard; ventilated front seats and heated rear seats are available.

New top-performance dual-motor F SPORT trim for 2026, replacing the prior 450e as RZ's flagship (402 total system hp). Adds Mark Levinson 13-speaker audio, a head-up display, and Panoramic View Monitor over 350e/450e. No frunk. 10-80% DC fast charge takes about 30 minutes. Battery warranty is 10 years / 150,000 miles.

Lucid states ~17 minutes to add 200 miles of DC charging for Pure, without a peak kW figure (Touring is rated 250 kW, Grand Touring 300 kW, on larger/higher-voltage packs). Uses DreamDrive advanced driver assistance (Level 2); DreamDrive Pro hands-free highway assist is an optional upgrade, not a self-driving system. Charge port is CCS1 — no native NACS port as of the 2026 model year.

819 hp / 885 lb-ft, 900V+ platform, up to 300 kW DC charging. 20-way power/ventilated/massage front seats standard. Lucid's current configurator lists a higher starting price reflecting a newer model-year update; $112,400 shown here is the 2025 model-year price.

3-row/7-seat configuration. EPA range varies 386-450 mi depending on wheel size (20"-23") and 2-row vs. 3-row configuration; 437 mi shown here is for the 3-row layout on standard 20"F/21"R wheels. Ground clearance is adjustable via air suspension (roughly 5.2-9.3 in), so no single figure is published. DreamDrive Pro is a supervised highway driver-assist package, not an unsupervised self-driving product.

US market gets only the dual-motor AWD variant (badged SE ALL4) — the lower-power single-motor FWD 'Countryman E' sold in Europe isn't offered here. EPA range is 212 mi on standard 18-inch wheels, 204 mi on optional 19-inch wheels. The new-generation MINI Cooper SE (Hardtop) electric hatchback isn't currently sold in the US (China-built, blocked by tariffs as of 2025-2026).

Compact 3-row SUV: optional 3rd-row seat brings capacity to 7 (base configuration is 5-seat/2-row). 250+ is single-motor FWD; AWD available on 300 4MATIC/350 4MATIC trims. Not rated for towing in the US. Mercedes does not offer a purchasable self-driving subscription on this model.
Top-trim dual-motor AWD EQB. Optional 3rd-row seat brings capacity to 7 (base configuration is 5-seat/2-row). Not rated for towing in the US.
No 3rd-row option on the EQE SUV.

No 3rd-row option on the EQE SUV (unlike the smaller EQB). 4MATIC (AWD) versions are rated to tow up to 3,500 lb; this RWD 350+ isn't officially tow-rated. Ground clearance varies 6.5-7.5 in with adaptive air suspension.

Single-motor RWD base sedan. No frunk. Not rated for towing. For 2025 the 350+ and 500 4MATIC use an updated 96-kWh battery pack; the 350 4MATIC retains the prior 90.6-kWh pack. Full Driving Assistance Package (enhanced semi-autonomous highway assist) is optional, not standard.
Top-trim dual-motor AWD sedan; optional MBUX Hyperscreen dashboard. No frunk. Not rated for towing.
Top dual-motor AWD, 3-row SUV trim. Optional 3rd-row seat brings capacity to 7 (base is 5-seat/2-row).

3-row SUV; optional 3rd-row seat brings capacity to 7 (base is 5-seat/2-row), though the 3rd row is snug — best suited to children or short trips. 450+ is single-motor RWD; AWD is available on 450 4MATIC/580 4MATIC. 4MATIC versions are rated to tow up to 3,500 lb.

Flagship electric sedan; liftback trunk design (22 cu ft with seats up, 63 cu ft with rear seats folded), no frunk. Mercedes offers a conditional SAE Level 3 'Drive Pilot' hands-off highway assist as a paid subscription on select EQS Sedan models, but only on limited freeways in California and Nevada under specific conditions — not a nationwide, always-available self-driving feature.
Top dual-motor AWD sedan trim. The same conditional Level 3 'Drive Pilot' hands-off highway assist applies as the 450+ — a CA/NV highway-only paid subscription, not a broad self-driving product.

2025 was the final model year the Ariya was built for the US — Nissan paused production ahead of MY2026 to reallocate resources to the redesigned Leaf, though the pause isn't (yet) a permanent cancellation; the vehicle remains sold from existing dealer inventory. FWD isn't tow-rated. ProPILOT Assist is standard; ProPILOT Assist 2.0 with hands-off highway driving is reserved for higher trims — not full self-driving.

Range-topping AWD trim with Nappa leather and a hands-free power liftgate; 19-inch wheels shown (267 mi EPA range), 20-inch wheel option drops range to 257 mi. 2025 was the final model year the Ariya was built for the US — Nissan paused production for MY2026 to focus on the redesigned Leaf. ProPILOT Assist 2.0 (hands-on-wheel highway assist) is standard on this trim but isn't a self-driving product.

All-new, redesigned third-generation Leaf switches from hatchback to crossover styling; entry trim of the fall-2026 launch lineup (S+, SV+, Platinum+). A lower-cost base 'S' grade with a smaller 52 kWh battery is planned to follow later, but isn't on sale yet. All launch trims share the same 75 kWh battery and 214 hp FWD motor; S+ has adaptive cruise as an option rather than standard, and ProPILOT Assist (lane centering) is standard only on SV+/Platinum+. Dual charge ports: NACS (DC fast charge, passenger fender) plus a J1772 Level 2 port on the driver's side.

All-new, redesigned third-generation Leaf switches from hatchback to crossover styling. SV+ adds standard ProPILOT Assist (adaptive cruise + lane centering), heated front seats, wireless phone charging, and two extra rear USB-C ports over S+. Shares the 75-kWh battery/214-hp FWD motor with all other 2026 launch trims. Dual charge ports: NACS (DC fast charge) plus J1772 Level 2.

Polestar's US configurator currently lists only the Long Range Dual Motor with Performance Pack for sale — this Single Motor RWD was EPA-certified for MY2025 and remains available in other markets, but current US pricing isn't published. No Android Auto — Polestar runs Android Automotive OS built-in rather than phone projection.

models.trim: Long Range Dual Motor with Performance Pack
models.notes: The only Polestar 2 configuration currently sold new in the US (Performance Pack standard, $64,800). 20-inch Performance forged wheels are standard.
No wireless phone charging. Rear seat heating requires the Performance Pack or Plus Pack.

models.trim: Long Range Dual Motor Performance Pack AWD
models.notes: 671 lb-ft torque with Performance Pack software. 22" Performance wheels standard. Bowers & Wilkins 1,610W/25-speaker audio standard.
No conventional rear windshield; uses a rear-facing camera/digital mirror instead. Frunk is a small 0.5 cu ft bin rather than a full front trunk. Rear seat heating requires the Plus Pack.
506 lb-ft torque. Dual 200 kW motors, 100 kWh gross/cell-to-pack battery.
Shares the PPE platform and 800V architecture with the Audi Q6 e-tron. Ground clearance varies 6.1-8.8 in with adaptive air suspension drive mode; 7.3 in is the standard figure.
Top Macan Electric trim: 630 hp / 833 lb-ft dual-motor. Curb weight is approximately 5,393 lb.

Base Taycan is a standard 4-seat configuration. Ships with an 89 kWh gross (~82 kWh usable) 'Performance Battery'; the larger 105 kWh gross (~97 kWh usable) 'Performance Battery Plus' is optional and raises range to 318 mi. Adaptive cruise control (InnoDrive) is an optional package, not standard. The redesigned 2025 model gets a new heat pump as standard equipment. Not tow-rated in the US.

938 hp / 2.3s 0-60 require the optional Sport Chrono push-to-pass launch control (up from 750 hp on the prior generation). Ships standard with the larger 97 kWh usable Performance Battery Plus and 21-inch Aero-Design wheels.

3-row SUV; no captain's-chairs option in MY2025 (added for MY2027), so the 2nd-row bench gives 7-passenger seating. Rides on adjustable air suspension (roughly 8.3-14.6 in of travel depending on mode), so no single ground-clearance figure is published. Vegan/synthetic interior materials only — no leather offered. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support. Rivian's 'Highway Assist' is a hands-on/limited hands-free driver-assist feature, not full self-driving.

Top performance trim: four independently-controlled motors, 1,025 hp / 1,198 lb-ft, sub-2.6s 0-60 (2.5s possible with 22-inch Super Sport wheels + Launch mode). Range is Rivian's own claim for the shared 140 kWh Max pack. Same cargo, seating, and interior-material notes as the Dual-Motor Large Pack entry apply.

Pickup truck with no conventional enclosed rear cargo/trunk area. Storage comes from an 11 cu ft powered frunk, an 11.7 cu ft 'Gear Tunnel' running through the cabin (65 in L x 18.1 in W x 20.3 in H, doors on both ends), and a 54.2 in long truck bed (51.1 in wide, extendable to 83.6 in with the tailgate down and seats folded). Adjustable air suspension means no single ground-clearance figure is published. Vegan/synthetic interior materials only; no Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support.

Rivian originally targeted late 2026 for Premium deliveries; company statements now point to early 2027 with no confirmed month. The 330-mile range is Rivian's own quoted figure for Premium, which shares Performance's battery pack. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto on any Rivian model.

Deliveries with the Launch Package began June 9, 2026. Rivian's optional Autonomy+ hands-free highway driving system costs $2,500 one-time or $49.99/month. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto on any Rivian model. Tow rating requires the Tow Package (standard in Launch Package).
Solterra is AWD-only across the entire US lineup (no FWD variant), unlike its mechanical twin the Toyota bZ4X. Uses StarTex synthetic upholstery, not genuine leather.
Touring adds a panoramic moonroof, heated and ventilated front seats, a digital rearview mirror, and smart key access on all five doors over Premium. AWD-only, no FWD option in the US.

Base tier of Tesla's current 3-tier trim naming (AWD / Premium AWD / Cyberbeast). Priced at $69,990. Tow capacity is 11,000 lb. No enclosed rear cargo hold — storage is a composite bed with a lockable tonneau cover; Tesla hasn't published an official frunk cubic-foot figure despite the Cybertruck having front trunk storage. Rides on 18-inch wheels with textile (non-leather) seats and coil-spring suspension (no adaptive air suspension, unlike Premium/Cyberbeast). Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is subscription-only at $99/month (no one-time purchase option). Battery warranty for the structural battery pack is 8 years/150,000 miles. DC fast charge ceiling is 350 kW, Level 2 AC is 11.5 kW; Vehicle-to-Load ('Powershare') supports continuous 9.6 kW output.

No enclosed rear cargo hold; Tesla hasn't published an official frunk cubic-foot figure. Cyberbeast is the tri-motor performance flagship: 845 hp / ~1,030 lb-ft, 2.6s 0-60, standard on 20-inch wheels with adaptive air suspension (so ground clearance varies and no single figure is published). Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is subscription-only at $99/month, available on Cyberbeast.

Tesla doesn't officially publish battery capacity, horsepower, 0-60 time, top speed, tow rating, or ground clearance for this model — those figures here are third-party estimates. MSRP, range, and MPGe are official EPA/manufacturer figures.
Battery capacity is a third-party estimate — Tesla doesn't officially publish it. Horsepower figures for Model 3 Performance vary by source (460-510 hp cited).

Model X has 'falcon wing' rear doors (roof-hinged, powered) rather than conventional or sliding doors. Seating can be 5, 6, or 7 depending on configuration (a 2+3+2 seven-seat layout is optional); this entry assumes the 6-seat (2+2+2) captain's-chair layout common on Plaid.
This is the 18-inch-wheel EPA rating (321 mi); a 19-inch-wheel variant is rated slightly lower. Battery capacity is a third-party estimate — Tesla doesn't officially publish it.

Tesla renamed this trim tier mid-2026 — Long Range Standard/AWD became Premium RWD/Premium AWD (a label change, not a spec change). Battery capacity is a third-party estimate — Tesla doesn't officially publish pack capacity.

Uses the smaller 57.7 kWh base battery (the bigger 74.7 kWh pack is reserved for XLE Plus/Limited trims). Renamed from bZ4X to 'bZ' for MY2026 as part of a facelift with a new front/rear fascia. Switched from CCS1 to a native NACS port; DC fast-charge ceiling is standardized at 150 kW across trims (was split 150/100 kW FWD/AWD on the old bZ4X), and Level 2 AC charging increased to 11 kW (was 6.6 kW). Toyota's current trim ladder is XLE / XLE Plus / Limited, each FWD or AWD.

AWD dual-motor, 338 hp combined — a meaningful power jump from the old bZ4X Limited AWD's 214 hp. DC fast-charge is unified at 150 kW (the old bZ4X AWD was capped at 100 kW). Renamed from bZ4X to 'bZ' for MY2026 as part of a facelift with a new front/rear fascia; switched from CCS1 to native NACS, and Level 2 AC charging increased to 11 kW (was 6.6 kW).

VF8 is sold only as a dual-motor AWD vehicle in the US — no single-motor RWD trim is offered. 10-year/125,000-mile vehicle warranty, longer than most competitors'. Seats are vegan (synthetic) leather, not genuine.
Plus trim adds power (402 hp vs. 349 hp on Eco) but has slightly less EPA range (235 vs. 256 mi). 20-inch wheels vs. Eco's 19-inch.
3-row, 7-passenger flagship SUV. The Eco trim (349 hp, EPA-rated 330 mi) starts around $62,900. Seats are vegan (synthetic) leather, not genuine.

MSRP excludes the $1,550 destination charge (total $61,545). No frunk — the front compartment holds only the washer-fluid reservoir, no cargo space. Front seats get heating, ventilation, and massage as standard. No built-in/integrated booster seat option.

MSRP excludes the $1,550 destination charge (total $70,540). VW's own spec sheet lists 0-60 mph as 6.0s; Car and Driver's independent test clocked this AWD trim at 5.5s. No frunk. Captain's-chair 2nd row seats 6 total, vs. the RWD Pro S's 7-passenger bench seat.

62 kWh is the gross/nominal pack size published for the Standard trim. Wireless charging, ventilated seats, heated steering wheel, and heat pump are Pro/Pro S-tier features, not standard here. VW discontinued this 62 kWh Standard trim for MY2026 — 2025 is the last model year it's offered.

82 kWh is the gross/nominal pack size published for Pro/Pro S trims. MY2025 got a mid-cycle AWD power bump to 335 hp (up from 295 hp in 2023-24). Includes 12-way power/massaging front seats and a panoramic glass roof.
The C40 Recharge was renamed EC40 in 2024. Part of the current MY2026 US lineup alongside EX30/EX40/EX90. Uses the 79 kWh-usable 'Extended Range' battery as the standard 'Single Motor' configuration.
Priced the same as the Single Motor RWD trim ($64,995) — unusual, but plausible if Volvo prices the top-equipped configuration of each drivetrain identically.

EX30 uses a fully leather-free interior across all trims (recycled/vegan materials) by design. No Android Auto — the infotainment system runs Google built-in (Android Automotive OS) natively; wireless Apple CarPlay is supported. Charge port is CCS1; Volvo has signaled a move to native NACS in the 2025-2026 timeframe.

EX30 uses a fully leather-free interior across all trims (recycled/vegan materials) by design. No Android Auto — the infotainment system runs Google built-in (Android Automotive OS) natively; wireless Apple CarPlay is supported. Charge port is CCS1, pending Volvo's move to native NACS.

All-new 2027 model; US order bank opened May 18, 2026, deliveries expected summer 2026. Pilot Assist (adaptive cruise + lane centering) is standard on the Plus trim. Nordico (vegan) upholstery is standard on Plus; leather (Nappa) and ventilated seats are Ultra-trim/option items. Heated rear seats and built-in rear booster cushions are Ultra-trim features, not standard on Plus. Battery warranty is 10 years to 80% capacity (no mileage cap published).

All-new 2027 model; US order bank opened May 18, 2026, deliveries expected summer 2026. Pilot Assist (adaptive cruise + lane centering) is standard on the Plus trim. Nordico (vegan) upholstery is standard on Plus; leather (Nappa) and ventilated seats are Ultra-trim/option items. Heated rear seats and built-in rear booster cushions are Ultra-trim features, not standard on Plus. Battery warranty is 10 years to 80% capacity. A higher-output P12 AWD configuration (112 kWh, 670 hp) is also planned.

Volvo offers 6- and 7-seat configurations; figures shown are for the 7-seat layout. Range varies by wheel size (up to 305 mi on 21" wheels standard on the Plus trim; 298 mi on 20"/22" wheels). Upholstery is Nordico (vegan) or wool blend; Volvo does not offer leather on the EX90. 800V architecture supports up to 350 kW DC and adds bidirectional Vehicle-to-Home/Vehicle-to-Grid capability.

Ultra trim rides on 22" wheels standard, which lowers EPA range slightly versus the Plus/21" figure. Front-seat massage and ventilated/perforated Nordico upholstery are standard on Ultra. MY26 update raised Performance output to 680 hp (from ~510 hp previously) via the new 800V architecture.

First Ford EV commercial van in this dataset. Represents the base Low Roof, standard-wheelbase Cargo Van RWD configuration; Medium/High Roof and Extended-length body options exist with up to 487.3 cu ft cargo, but Low Roof is the highest-volume fleet configuration. Seats only the driver and front passenger (no rear seats in a cargo van). BlueCruise isn't offered on E-Transit. Native CCS1 charge port, with an optional NACS adapter for Supercharger access. Historically RWD-only.

SUV body style, distinct from the Hummer EV Pickup 3X — shares the same tri-motor 1,000 hp drivetrain and Ultium platform, but has an enclosed rear cargo hold (35.9 cu ft, 81.7 cu ft with seats folded) instead of a bed. Native NACS charge port.

Listed as its own model ('Ioniq 5 N') rather than a trim of Ioniq 5, matching how Hyundai and reviewers treat the N line — distinct chassis tuning and unique wide-body fender flares. Starting price is $59,900 (a $6,300 cut for MY2026, down from $66,200). 641 hp is the peak figure with N Grin Boost (a 10-second overboost mode); continuous rated output is 601 hp. 0-60 of 3.25s is likewise the N Grin Boost figure. Shares its 84 kWh usable battery with the standard Ioniq 5 AWD. Switched to a native NACS charge port for MY2026, matching the rest of the Ioniq 5 lineup. Ride height is lowered about 20mm versus standard Ioniq 5.

New sedan nameplate on Audi's PPE platform (shared with Q6 e-tron/Porsche Macan Electric), sold in the US as the A6 Sportback e-tron (fastback body). Single rear motor base trim. Level 2 charging is 11 kW. Cargo figure (39.9 cu ft) is with the rear seats folded.

New sedan nameplate on Audi's PPE platform (shared with Q6 e-tron/Porsche Macan Electric), sold in the US as the A6 Sportback e-tron (fastback body). Level 2 charging is 11 kW. Cargo figure (39.9 cu ft) is with the rear seats folded.

Electric G-Wagen: four individually-controlled motors (one per wheel), retains the ladder-frame chassis, three locking differentials, and real off-road hardware (G-Turn tank-turn maneuver on loose surfaces, G-Steering reduced turning radius). Not available with a tow hitch in the US. No usable frunk — the space under the hood isn't configured as cargo, consistent with the gas G-Class. Single US configuration (no separate lower trim).

Mercedes' first EV on the new MB.EA platform — distinct from the EQB/EQE/EQS entries (those are on EVA2, this is a smaller/newer architecture). An 85 kWh battery with a new silicon-oxide-blend anode gives an unusually long 374-mile EPA range for the battery size. Base trim seats are MB-Tex synthetic leather, not genuine. First Mercedes-Benz with a native NACS DC fast-charging port standard from the factory (paired with a separate J1772 port for AC) — comes standard with an included CCS-to-NACS adapter for accessing non-Tesla CCS networks too.

Mercedes' first EV on the new MB.EA platform — distinct from the EQB/EQE/EQS entries (those are on EVA2, this is a smaller/newer architecture). New full-size electric SUV body style for Porsche (larger than the Macan Electric), on sale since March 2026. EPA range isn't yet certified — Porsche and reviewers cite WLTP-based estimates in the 300-340 mile range, but no official EPA figure has been published yet. All trims are dual-motor AWD, no RWD option. Ground clearance varies 6.9-9.6 in across the adaptive air suspension's four ride-height modes; 7.5 in ('Normal' mode) is shown here. First Porsche with a native NACS DC fast-charging port (paired with a separate J1772 port for AC) — comes standard with an included NACS-to-CCS1 adapter for accessing non-Tesla CCS networks too.

New full-size electric SUV body style for Porsche (larger than the Macan Electric), on sale since March 2026. EPA range isn't yet certified — Porsche and reviewers cite WLTP-based estimates in the 300-340 mile range, but no official EPA figure has been published yet. All trims are dual-motor AWD, no RWD option. Ground clearance varies 6.9-9.6 in across the adaptive air suspension's four ride-height modes; 7.5 in ('Normal' mode) is shown here. First Porsche with a native NACS DC fast-charging port (paired with a separate J1772 port for AC) — comes standard with an included NACS-to-CCS1 adapter for accessing non-Tesla CCS networks too.
Ultra-luxury sub-brand tier of the EQS SUV (regular EQS SUV entries are badged Mercedes-Benz; this is Mercedes-Maybach, roughly 2-3x the regular EQS SUV's price). No frunk.

Third Subaru EV model alongside Solterra and Trailseeker (subcompact, below both in size/price) — Subaru's first FWD-based EV, on a different platform than the Toyota-shared Solterra. Base Premium trim is single-motor FWD only; AWD (dual-motor, 338 hp combined) is exclusive to Sport/GT trims. Not rated to tow on any trim. No frunk. Heat pump is standard on Sport/GT but not on this base Premium trim.

Third Subaru EV model alongside Solterra and Trailseeker (subcompact, below both in size/price) — Subaru's first FWD-based EV, on a different platform than the Toyota-shared Solterra. GT is the AWD (dual-motor, 338 hp combined) performance trim; base Premium is single-motor FWD only. Not rated to tow on any trim. No frunk. Heat pump is standard on Sport/GT trims.

Cheaper entry point below the Grand Touring — same Gravity body/platform but a smaller 89 kWh pack (vs. Grand Touring's 123 kWh) and single-tier motor output. Base configuration is the 5-seat/2-row layout (111.9 cu ft folded); a 7-seat/3-row option also exists (106.2 cu ft folded). Ground clearance is adjustable via air suspension, so no single figure is published.

Off-road-styled variant of the compact bZ (formerly bZ4X, renamed 'bZ' for MY2026), listed as its own model since Toyota markets Woodland as a distinct trim family. Standard AWD dual-motor, no FWD/single-motor option. Two EPA-certified range configurations exist depending on tire choice (235/60R18 = 281 mi used here, 235/65R18 = 260 mi). Woodland Premium adds heated and ventilated seats over this base Woodland grade.

Off-road-styled variant of the compact bZ (formerly bZ4X, renamed 'bZ' for MY2026), listed as its own model since Toyota markets Woodland as a distinct trim family. Standard AWD dual-motor, no FWD/single-motor option. Two EPA-certified range configurations exist depending on tire choice (235/60R18 = 281 mi used here, 235/65R18 = 260 mi). Adds heated and ventilated seats over the base Woodland grade.

2026 is Tesla's final model year for the current Model S generation. Both trims are now AWD-only — the older single-motor/RWD base configuration has been dropped. No factory tow rating (aftermarket hitches exist, rated around 2,000 lb weight-carrying, but that's not an official Tesla spec). No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support.

No factory tow rating (aftermarket hitches exist, rated around 2,000 lb weight-carrying, but that's not an official Tesla spec). No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support.

New long-wheelbase 3-row/6-seat variant of Model Y, launched July 2026 — a genuinely different body style from the standard 2-row Model Y, not just a trim/package. Horsepower (444 hp) is computed from Tesla's published combined motor output (194 kW rear + 137 kW front); Tesla doesn't publish an official combined hp figure directly. Cargo figures differ from the standard 2-row Model Y due to the stretched 3-row body; frunk and tow rating are shared with the standard Model Y.
Base (non-Plaid) Model X trim. Falcon-wing rear doors (roof-hinged, powered) rather than conventional or sliding doors. Assumes the 6-seat (2+2+2 captain's-chair) layout common on Model X.
